paragraphs.text: Congenital myasthenic syndrome-11 (CMS11) is an autosomal recessive postsynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission. It is caused by deficiency of the acetylcholine receptor (AChR) at the endplate, which results from defects in rapsyn, a postsynaptic protein needed to cluster AChR at the endplate (Ohno et al., 2002; Dunne and Maselli, 2004). Most patients present in the first year of life, sometimes with arthrogryposis and respiratory crises, but some present later (Burke et al., 2003; Engel et al., 2015). Most patients respond well to acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors (Engel et al., 2015).

paragraphs.text: Goldhammer et al. (1990) described 14 Jewish patients from 10 families of Iraqi or Iranian origin who had congenital myasthenia with associated facial malformations. The facial malformations were an elongated face, mandibular prognathism with class III malocclusion, and a high-arched palate. Muscle weakness was mainly restricted to ptosis, weakness of the facial and masticatory muscles, and fatigable speech. The course was mild and nonprogressive, and the patients responded to cholinesterase inhibitors. None had antibodies to the acetylcholine receptor. Repetitive stimulation at 3 Hz produced a decremental response, but a single nerve stimulus did not produce a repetitive compound muscle action potential.

paragraphs.text: Ohno et al. (2003) found E-box mutations in the RAPSN promoter region in 8 patients with CMS. Patient 1 carried a -27C-G mutation, which changes an E-box at positions -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG. The allele carrying this mutation was not transcribed in the patient's muscle. Patients 2 to 8 were Oriental Jews of Iraqi or Iranian origin with facial malformations. They carried a -38A-G mutation, which changes another E-box at positions -40 to -35 from CAACTG to CAGCTG and does not affect the consensus CANNTG sequence. In electrophoretic mobility shift assays, the -38A-G mutation gained binding affinity, and the -27C-G mutation lost binding affinity, for different components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts. Both mutations reduced reporter expression in C2C12 myotubes. The -27C-G mutation also reduced expression in HEK cells transfected with MyoD or myogenin, and it markedly reduced the enhancer activity of an E-box on an SV40 promoter. Ohno et al. (2003) also determined that the major transcriptional start site of RAPSN lies 172 nucleotides upstream of the translational start site.
